item: key files: every name change is flushed to its folder, and a wrap in flight can no longer undo an erase
summary: OPEN_QUEUE 2026-10-27 list item 41(c), verified on main 3429b18a before the fix. BEFORE: keyfile.replace_in_place and create_new flushed the key's bytes but never the keys folder, so a power cut right after a plaintext key was wrapped in place could bring the PLAINTEXT file back under its name (and the removed plaintext alias back in keys/.pending), on exactly the switched-off machine the at-rest encryption is for; and the check that the file was still the one read and the os.replace that acted on it were two steps that quick_crypto_erase, which took no lock, could fall between, so a wrap in flight put the destroyed key back (wrapped) after the erase had counted it destroyed. NOW: file_lock.flush_folder (A-030's folder flush, now public) runs after every rename, link and alias removal of a key file; a flush failure is logged by class and never turns a done replace into a refusal. One process-level lock, keyfile.KEY_FILES_LOCK, is held across the check and the replace, across the link of a creation, and by the erase from its key step to the removal of the data folder; a wrap that waited finds its file gone and stands down, and a creation after the erase makes a new key, never the destroyed one. Stated limit: another process on the same data folder is not covered by the lock (as before for the identity check). tests/test_key_file_durability.py: 6 tests, all red on the old code. Release-notes line: «Encryption keys are now flushed to disk when they are created or re-wrapped, so a power cut can no longer bring back an unencrypted copy, and an emergency erase can no longer be undone by a key re-wrap that was running at the same moment.»
